Definition: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to G5259 through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor:--sleep.
BiblicalUsage: hýpnos is a plain word for sleep, slumber. In Matthew 1:24, the text says "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him." In Luke 9:32, the text says "But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hýpnos matters because rest is God's gift, not a reward for finishing — He rested, and He invites us to. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; Raising of Lazarus; The Angel Appears to Joseph
